name: Royal Oak
description: Identify the Royal Oak by its octagonal bezel secured with eight exposed hexagonal screws, the 'Tapisserie' waffle-textured dial, and the integrated tapering bracelet. It may come in variants like: blue 'Petite Tapisserie' dial, grey, black, and openworked skeleton dials.

name: Royal Oak Offshore
description: Identify the Royal Oak Offshore as a bigger, bolder Royal Oak: a thicker case, an oversized screwed octagonal bezel, a 'Méga Tapisserie' dial, chunky chronograph pushers, and often a rubber strap. It may come in variants like: black, blue, and camouflage editions.

name: Royal Oak Concept
description: Identify the Royal Oak Concept as the avant-garde Royal Oak: an oversized, sculpted octagonal case (often ceramic or titanium) with a fully openworked, skeletonised dial. Look for the exposed movement, a floating tourbillon cage, and unconventional displays like the 'H-N-R' (Hour/Neutral/Winding) selector and a jumping-hour or power-reserve window, all on a rubber strap.

name: Code 11.59
description: Identify the Code 11.59 by its round bezel set within a clearly visible octagonal middle case, a double-curved sapphire crystal, and a stick-style applied logo. It may come in variants like: blue lacquer dial, black, white, and smoked editions.

name: Millenary
description: Identify this Millenary by its clean round case ringed with a full set of luminous Arabic numerals, a slim date window at 3 o'clock, dauphine hands, and 'AUTOMATIC' script above six. A restrained, legible dress piece rather than a sports watch.

name: Jules Audemars
description: Identify the Jules Audemars as AP's purest dress watch: a slim, perfectly round case with a thin polished bezel, a guilloché-textured dial with fine applied baton indices, and slender hands. Minimal and time-only — no date, no sub-dials — the antithesis of the Royal Oak.

name: Edward Piguet
description: Identify the Edward Piguet by its upright rectangular (tonneau) case — unusual for AP. This chronograph carries a black dial with three sub-dials, Arabic numerals at the quarters, a date window, chronograph pushers on the right, and the 'AP' monogram above centre.
